description:
`src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs` must not turn absent semantic evidence or an invalid transport position into `any`. `any` is a real top fact, not a placeholder for “not computed” or “this position does not exist”; once admitted to a cumulative answer it cannot be retracted (the fz-f98.17 defect class).

At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, eleven position-type paths still silently choose `any`:

1. `generic_owner_ty_and_demand`: `ExecutableInput` with no input at `semantic_index`.
2. `generic_owner_ty_and_demand`: `Value` with no analyzed value type.
3. `generic_owner_ty_and_demand`: `CallArg` with no source arg or no analyzed arg type.
4. `generic_owner_ty_and_demand`: `ResumePayload` with no delivered-resume value or no analyzed value type.
5. `produce_local_callable_construction`: local callable producer with no analyzed value type.
6. `produce_local_callable_construction`: local callable capture with no analyzed value type.
7. `produce_named_transport_position`: `ExecutableInput` with no input at `semantic_index`.
8. `produce_named_transport_position`: `Value` with no analyzed value type.
9. `produce_named_transport_position`: `CallArg` with no source arg (the direct `let ty = any()` branch).
10. `produce_named_transport_position`: present `CallArg` with no analyzed arg type.
11. `produce_named_transport_position`: delivered `ReturnPayload` with no analyzed result type.

This census deliberately excludes the `exact_tuple_field_tys` fallbacks used while projecting a non-exact tuple shape; those answer a different shape-projection question and are not missing position/value evidence.

The sharpest contradiction is `ResumePayload`: the generic-owner arm manually performs a permissive lookup and returns `any`, while the named-position arm calls `resume_payload_ty`, which requires a delivered-resume entry and an analyzed type. One position kind cannot have two type authorities. Collapse both paths onto the strict derivation.

Use the semantic output-contract loop, not blind replacement:

- Give each of the eleven paths a separately identifiable temporary probe (panic or equivalent test-only telemetry), including enough executable/position/value identity to explain a hit.
- Run `cargo test --lib` and `cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1`; record hit counts per semantic site.
- A zero-hit fallback is dead and becomes a named invariant with a precise failure message. A hit requires a smallest production-boundary regression and a trace to the first missing/wrong fact. If the position is dead or invalid, represent that fact (`none`, no position, or an invariant as appropriate); retain `any` only where the runtime value is genuinely dynamic and document/test why it is earned.
- Share derivation helpers wherever generic-owner and named-position paths answer the same question. At minimum, both `ResumePayload` paths must call the same strict helper; also resolve the generic/named `CallArg` disagreement about absent source args.
- Remove all temporary probes/scaffolding after the proof. Update `.agent/docs/semantic-fixpoint.md` and `.agent/docs/pipeline.md` if the authority or legitimate-`any` model changes.

Acceptance:

- All eleven sites are removed, converted to explicit invariants/dead-position handling, or retain `any` with a concrete semantic justification and focused regression evidence.
- `ResumePayload` has one type derivation.
- An absent `CallArg` source/index cannot silently become `any`.
- No temporary probes remain.
- `cargo test --lib` and the single-threaded fixture matrix pass at baseline or better, with warnings treated as failures.
title: Audit the eleven silent any position-type defaults in transport.rs
